chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Two rak'ahs prayed by a married man are better than seventy rak'ahs prayed by a bachelor.'
A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.أَعْزَبُ: The bachelor — an unmarried adult male. The term carries connotations of incompleteness of religious duty in classical hadith literature.
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Better/superior in merit — a comparative adjective used to express spiritual excellence or greater reward.
key_terms.الْمُتَزَوِّجُ: The married man — one who has entered into a valid Islamic marriage contract (nikah).
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: Two rak'ahs — a rak'ah (pl. raka'at) is a unit of Islamic ritual prayer (salat), consisting of standing, bowing, prostration, and recitation.

ai.seo_question: Why does Islam encourage marriage? What is the spiritual reward of marriage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that marriage elevates the spiritual value of prayer: two rak'ahs prayed by a married person surpass seventy rak'ahs prayed by a bachelor. This hadith is transmitted via two independent chains to reinforce its authority. In classical Shia jurisprudence, this teaching was understood as a strong encouragement for Muslims to marry, linking the fulfillment of a social and religious obligation with an amplification of one's acts of worship.
word_analysis: similar to it / the like of it

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Al Qadah who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two Cycles Prayed by the married (man) is better than seventy Cycles Prayed by the bachelor’.
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Two Rak’at Salat (prayer) performed by a married person is more virtuous than seventy Rak’at Salat (prayer) performed by a non-married person.’”
“A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.”
